definition: distinct species x gene x site codon calls in the atlas, whatever the species carries at that site
note: DECLARED HEADLINE for atlas size; this is what the abstract quotes as codon calls. A long-format row count is a different quantity and must not be quoted in its place.

definition: distinct species x gene x site codon calls where the species is wild-type at that site
note: The subset the null pools are built from, because a species that is not wild-type at a site contributes no codon to that site's pool. This is the 23,978 reported by step9_01.

definition: distinct species x gene x site codon calls where the species is not wild-type at that site
note: The complement. 25,574 minus 23,978; the reason the two scripts appeared to disagree.

definition: rows of codon_atlas.csv carrying is_wildtype == True
note: NOT a count of codon calls. One row per curated allele at a site, so this is a property of how much literature exists per site. Never quote it as atlas size.

definition: rows of codon_atlas.csv in all, wild-type and not
note: The size of Dataset S1. The wild-type subset of it is n_atlas_rows_long_format; quoting one for the other conflates the dataset with the part of it the core test uses.

definition: distinct species carrying at least one codon call
distinct gene LABELS in the atlas
note: NOT the number of genes. GluCl_Px and GluCl_Tu are two sites on one GluCl gene, not two genes: ortho01 finds them on the same protein accession in 236 of 569 species and at a near-constant offset of +6 residues in 352 of them. Never quote this as a gene count.

definition: distinct target GENES in the atlas, after merging the two GluCl labels
note: DECLARED HEADLINE for the gene count: six, not the seven gene LABELS. The site count is unaffected. Leave-one-gene-out that drops GluCl_Px or GluCl_Tu separately is dropping one SITE, not one gene, and must be described that way.

definition: distinct gene x site pairs in the atlas
curated resistance events entering the core test
events where the SITE x ALLELE supply fraction is strictly between 0 and 1 -- some but not all panel species could reach that allele there
note: The 48. A property of the site, not of the species.

definition: events where every panel species could reach the allele (supply = 1)
events where no panel species could reach the allele (supply = 0)
events where THAT SPECIES' OWN codon reaches some but not all of the alleles curated at that site, so it can tell them apart
method: step3_03 TEST 2, one row per event
note: The 32. A property of the species' codon, not of the site. NOT a subset relation with the 48 -- a different question.

definition: events whose observed allele was not one nucleotide step from the species' wild-type codon
note: Verified identical to the supply-zero stratum, not assumed.

definition: breaches that fall inside the codon-discriminating subset
note: One breach (Ctenocephalides felis VGSC T929 ACG->V) reaches NONE of the site repertoire, so its codon cannot discriminate and TEST 2 excludes it by construction. The difference is definitional, not a missing event.

definition: sum of per-event accessibility probabilities under the atlas-pool null
note: CANONICAL. Permutation budgets give 84.68-84.71; those estimate this number, they do not compete with it. Quote the exact value.

definition: observed accessible / expected accessible, all events
method: ratio of the two rows above
note: CANONICAL. Must equal observed/expected_null_pooled at full precision. This is NOT the headline result of the paper -- see the note at the end.

definition: site-level odds that an observed allele is accessible, conditional logit with site fixed effects, adjusted for ESM-2 predicted effect
note: DECLARED HEADLINE. The most conservative of the five and the one that survives the 'this is just protein-level tolerance' objection, because ESM-2 is in the model. Quoting the smallest defensible effect is the stronger position; the other four go in the robustness panel.

note: DECLARED HEADLINE. order x site and family x site add phylogenetic strata and move it to 13.27 and 11.18 -- report as robustness.

definition: same estimand, additionally stratified
note: robustness

definition: same estimand, additionally stratified
note: robustness

definition: species-level odds restricted by ascertainment subset
note: SAME ESTIMATOR as the headline at finer precision -- not a sixth estimate; the apparent multiplicity was a duplicate.

definition: species-level odds restricted by ascertainment subset
note: ascertainment robustness: the effect survives restriction

definition: exact stratified hypergeometric tail, conditioning on site margins
note: No odds ratio by construction. This is the assumption-free anchor: it makes no model of the effect, only of the margins. Quote it alongside the headline OR.

definition: exponent on mutational supply: P(allele observed) proportional to m^beta, m = kappa*transitions + transversions, ESM-2 adjusted
note: CANONICAL. beta=0 means supply is irrelevant; beta=1 means observation is proportional to supply. Quote with its interval, never alone.

definition: coefficient on ESM-2 predicted effect, per standard deviation
note: the protein-tolerance term that sits alongside beta in one model

definition: transition:transversion rate ratio, estimated not assumed
note: NOT a measurement of the arthropod ts:tv ratio. It is a nuisance parameter and its own profile is nearly flat. Do not quote it as biology.

value: 95% profile CI [0.0478, 1.1157] (bounds by bisection to 1e-4), gamma and kappa profiled out
definition: 95% profile interval for beta, gamma and kappa profiled out
method: profile likelihood, bounds located by bisection to 1e-4
note: CANONICAL interval. Bounds are a property of the likelihood, not of a grid step.

definition: does the 95% profile interval exclude beta = 0?
method: profile log-likelihood at beta=0 vs cutoff
note: 1 = yes. If 0, the manuscript must NOT claim the interval excludes zero.

definition: median beta over site-cluster bootstrap resamples
note: independent of the profile interval; CARRIED FORWARD from a previous run; 95% percentile [0.0016, 1.1066] over 2000 site resamp

definition: likelihood-ratio test of kappa = 2 against the co-estimated value
note: LR=1.0852 df=1 P=0.29753 for kappa=2.0 vs co-estimated 4.703; indistinguishable

definition: 95% profile interval for kappa itself
